newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr firm in Tokyo after brief rise over 114 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firm in Tokyo after brief rise over 114 yen.

text.p: *Dollar firm in mid-morning Tokyo after briefly rising to around 114.20 yen but then falling back on light U.S. fund sales and some interbank offers.

*Gains made largely on back of short-covering of marks for yen, with trust banks, who had sold heavily Tuesday, most active. Buying of marks for yen by Asian and U.S. operators also detected, with stop-loss buying also likely.
*Mark rose to around 67.95 yen before dropping to around 67.81/84 yen by 0128 GMT.

*Dealers said more stop-loss buying was possible. "We are likely to have stop-loss buying orders lined up around every 0.50 yen, with the next ones at 68.00 yen," one U.S. bank dealer said. Mark ended Tuesday Tokyo trade at 66.55 yen.
*Commercial buying of dollars ahead of 0100 GMT local fixing also detected, dealers said.

*Although dollar direction difficult to predict, dealers said sales on rallies still likely to keep topside weighted, but that any dips would invite bargain-hunting from operators who failed to buy dollar at lower levels on Tuesday. Dollar ended Tuesday New York trade at 112.58/68 yen.
*Dollar rose against yen, primarily on short-covering by interbank traders.
*Topside remained heavy at around 113.50 yen and relatively large amount of sales at around 113.35 yen briefly pushed dollar down to around 113.00 yen, dealers said.
*Talk of bids overnight by Japanese public fund at around 112.50 yen supporting dollar, one bank dealer.
*Fed's decision to leave interest rates steady already digested overnight and not seen as factor to push down dollar/yen further in Tokyo, dealers said.
*Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, was scheduled to speak at economic seminar but cancelled and will attend parliament instead.

*He said on Tuesday that pace of yen's strengthening too rapid and too much volatility in foreign exchange markets was undesirable and that Japan would "deal appropriately" with such excessive volatility.
*Dollar was bought in early Tokyo on speculation that Sakakibara may say something that would prevent yen from rising excessively against dollar, said a European bank dealer.
